Walmart SDE-3 Interview Experience

Recently interviewed for SDE-3 at Walmart. Sharing my experience in case it helps others.

Round 1 – DSA

Q1: Next Greater Element II

Q2: A grid-based problem similar to Walls and Gates / Rotting Oranges (classic BFS pattern)

➡️ Got confirmation from the recruiter that I cleared Round 1.

Round 2 – LLD + Java

This was my first Low-Level Design round, and honestly, I didn’t perform well here.

I was able to answer Java and Spring Boot–related questions confidently.

However, my LLD approach and structuring were not strong enough.

❌ Didn’t qualify for Round 3.

Takeaway

DSA alone isn’t enough for senior roles.

Strong LLD fundamentals are critical for SDE-3 and above.

Lesson learned — time to focus more on design patterns, object modeling, and clean design thinking.

Hope this helps someone preparing for similar roles. All the best! 🚀

title: Design a Delayed Webhook Retry Scheduler

reported.text: Design an in-memory structure for delayed webhook retries: scheduleRetry(eventId, executeAt) and getEventsToExecuteNow(now).

sources.passage:
Walmart SDE3 interview DS+coding round
Questions:
1. In backend systems, webhooks or payment callbacks often fail and need to be retried. Design an in-memory data structure to handle delayed retries.

When an event fails, it needs to be retried after a specific delay (e.g., 5 seconds, then 15 seconds, etc.).

Please explain the data structures you would use to implement these two methods efficiently: 
public void scheduleRetry(String eventId, long executeAtTimestamp)
public List<String> getEventsToExecuteNow(long currentTimestamp)

2. To prevent API abuse on a refund service, we need to implement an in-memory rate limiter for specific merchants.

The rule is: A merchant can only initiate 'K' refunds within a rolling 5-minute window.

Explain the data structures you would use to implement a method boolean allowRefund(String merchantId, long timestamp) that returns true if the refund is allowed, and false if they have exceeded their limit in the last 5 minutes."

The interviewer was kind enough to explain the question multiple times. It was medium level coding questions

title: Longest Substring With at Most K Vowels

reported.text: Length of the longest substring containing at most k vowels, tested on 15 cases; then logic puzzles.

This interview was special for me for many reasons.

I interviewed for an **SDE-2 role at Walmart**, and unlike most interviews post-COVID, this was a **fully in-person interview**. All rounds were scheduled on a **single Saturday**, back-to-back, at the Walmart office in **Bellandur, Bangalore**.

Since I belong to the **COVID batch (2018–2022)**, this was actually my **first-ever in-person interview**. No teams/zoom call. No mute button. Just real humans, whiteboards, and adrenaline.

Scary? Yes.  
Thrilling? Absolutely.

## Taking the Leap

When the recruiter mentioned it would be an in-person interview, my first instinct was hesitation. Online interviews had become my comfort zone.

But I took a deep breath and said **yes**.

I showed up at the Walmart office that Saturday morning, slightly nervous but excited to finally experience what interviews used to feel like pre-COVID.

And honestly — I’m glad I did.

## Round 1: DSA (Strings + Sliding Window)

The first round was **pure DSA**.

## Problem Statement (Simplified)

> *Given a string, find the length of the* ***longest substring*** *that contains* ***at most*** `k` ***vowels****.*

## My Approach

1. I started with a **brute-force approach**, explaining the idea clearly.
2. Then I optimized it to an **O(n)** solution using the **sliding window technique**.
3. I wrote **working code within the first 20 minutes**.

The problem itself was **medium-level**, but the interviewer didn’t stop there.

He:

* Added **edge cases**
* Asked how I’d tweak the logic for different constraints
* Tested my solution against **15 different test cases**

My solution passed all of them successfully.

Since there was still time left, he threw in a couple of **logic puzzles**, which turned the round into a surprisingly fun discussion.

**Outcome:** Strong start and high confidence going into the next round.

## Round 2: LLD — Designing a Live News Feed System

This round was **Low-Level Design focused**, but I intentionally approached it **top-down**.

Before jumping into classes, I explained how the system would work at a high level.

reported.text: Explain and implement HashMap internals, then design a browser that keeps at most 10 tabs open and closes the least recently used one when a new tab opens.

sources.passage:
Walmart | SDE3 | Bangalore | April 2025

**Interview Format & Experience**

**Round 1 – Technical (DSA) – 60 mins**

Quick self-introductions
Explain and implement the internal working of HashMap.
Design a browser system where only 10 tabs can stay open. When a new tab opens, the least recently used (LRU) tab should close. I had to explain the data structure, logic, and time complexity.
Discuss time complexities of common sorting algorithms.

**Round 2 – Low-Level Design (Java) – 60 mins**

Briefed my previous project
Asked to design BookMyShow: define classes, schemas, and explain concurrency handling.
Discussed relevant design patterns, why I’d use them, and gave a short explanation of each.
Some core Java questions:
Difference between Abstract class vs Interface
If abstract class has a constructor, why can't we instantiate it?

**Round 3 – Hiring Manager Round – 60 mins**

Again, started with project discussion
Behavioral questions like:
What are you most proud of?
What have you learned from experience (non-technical)?
How do you resolve issues?
Why are you looking to leave your current company?
Also covered:
Deployment process
SQL vs NoSQL
SDLC and methodology followed in current org

reported.text: Implement an in-memory file system with a root folder where folders contain folders or text files and you can list a folder's contents; plus Reorganize String.

sources.passage:
Walmart Global tech Staff Engineer IN5
# Round 1: DS + ALgo + Problem solving 1hr
2 leetcode medium problems
1. Given a string s, rearrange the characters of s so that any two adjacent characters are not the same.
2. Design inmemory file system
    *   There will be a root folder (RF)
    *   Each folder can contain either 0 or many folders or text files
    *   List all folders OR files given a particular Folder

# Round 2: HLD + LLD
**Design Tagging system.**
1. A web page can have multiple tags. 
2. User can create new tag if not present in the system or reuse. 
3. Need to fetch the tag with prefix typed by the user on realtime. 
4. Additional requirement get all the pages tagged by a tag. 
5. Get all the tags for a page. 
6. User should see his/her new tag in real time, while other user can see it with some delay.

# Round 3: System design
**Design rate limiter**
1. Rate limiter as saas product.
2. How to detect DDoS
3. How to detect Bot
Most of the time we spent on discussion technologies. Where to cache, why to use cache. Kafka queue and its internal implementation etc

# Round 4: Hiring Manager
1. Introduction
2. How do you review code based on given scenario. 
3. Many cross questions based on answer. QA testing, stg testing, how do you automate. 
3. Challanging project/things which you have done or something you have introduced new tech/things. What was the reason? How did you handle all stake holder. Challenges you faced.
4. Incident handling. How do you handle incidences. P0, P1 level incidences. Why do we need RCA(Root cause Analysis).
5. How do you motivate engineers/team member when they spent enough time to investigate things.
6. How do you start your day why you have things to deploy on Prod.
7. Motivation to join Walmart and many more
8. Lastly It was my turn to ask question I spent 15-20 min to discuss things like 
   * Development
   * Deployment flow. How do you deploy hotfix? 
   * Do you prefer changes being done/deploy asap make fix, test it thoroughly and then release.
   * How do you handle team members conflicts
   * work culture

I don't know what will come from HR but I really enjoyed interviews and discussion with panel. They ware very supportive and engaging.
Happy Hunting.. Good luck
